\[

\]  
The weight average molecular weight (M_w) requires calculating the mass contributions. For 1 mole of the mixture:  
- Mass of the first component: \(0.50 \times 100,000 = 50,000 \, \text{g}\),  
- Mass of the second component: \(0.50 \times 200,000 = 100,000 \, \text{g}\),  
- Total mass = \(50,000 + 100,000 = 150,000 \, \text{g}\).  

The weight fractions are:  
\[
w_1 = \frac{50,000}{150,000} = \frac{1}{3}, \quad w_2 = \frac{100,000}{150,000} = \frac{2}{3}.
\]  
Thus,  
\[
M_w = \left(\frac{1}{3} \times 100,000\right) + \left(\frac{2}{3} \times 200,000\right) = \frac{100,000}{3} + \frac{400,000}{3} = \frac{500,000}{3} \approx 166,666.67 \, \text{g/mol} \, (1.67 \times 10^5 \, \text{g/mol}).
\]

\[
0.3 \, \text{g/lb} \times 150 \, \text{lb} = 45 \, \text{g (body's requirement)},  
\]  
\[
\frac{45 \, \text{g}}{0.70} \approx 64.29 \, \text{g},  
\]  
which rounds to **64.5 g/day** (Option C). This matches the closest provided option.
